issues.failure_explanation: For any pair i,j the difference c_j-c_i satisfies a linear equation d/dt(c_j-c_i) = -(2/N)φ(r_ij)(c_j-c_i) (exactly so for N=2, and by Gronwall in general) with φ bounded (compact support); hence (c_j-c_i)(t) = (c_j-c_i)(0)·exp(-(2/N)∫_0^t φ(r_ij)) ≠ 0 at every finite t whenever c_i^0 ≠ c_j^0. Exact clusters (grey level exactly constant on a region) therefore form only as t→∞, not in finite time, and at any finite T the claimed 'constant' grey levels are only approximate.

failure_location.quote: Classical results for opinion dynamics models~\cite{MotschTadmor2014} ensure that, under mild assumptions on $\phi$, the solution converges to a finite number of clusters in finite time.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'converges to a finite number of clusters in finite time' by convergence as t→∞ (or by approximate clustering), and state that at finite T the grey level is only approximately constant on each cluster, matching the histograms actually produced.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the multi-agent dynamics delivers an exact colour quantization in finite time is unsupported; Remark rmk:parameters' advice that 'T should be large enough to enable the formation of clusters' and the interpretation of the computed images as quantizations hold only approximately.
issues.title: Finite-time formation of exact colour clusters is impossible for the stated dynamics
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local wording change but it necessarily withdraws the promised guarantee (exact clustering at finite time), so the conclusion is only left in weakened, approximate form; the method and experiments otherwise survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The two-way Armijo tests evaluate J at Π_E(ε-τD) against J(ε)-cτ|D|², i.e. they certify sufficient decrease for the step along -D (and with the terminal condition of eq:opt_system-b, D = ∂_εF·λ is exactly the gradient of ε↦J(c(·,T;ε)), so -D is the descent direction), yet the accepted update moves along +σD. Thus the step actually taken is the opposite of the step whose decrease was verified, and no monotonicity/descent guarantee holds. The sign convention is itself inconsistent in the derivation: varying the stated augmented cost J̃ = ∫λ[∂_t c - F] + J gives λ(T) = Δc(T) - α(c(T)-I(x)), the negative of the terminal condition stated in eq:opt_system-b (the appendix's own displayed computation implies that sign, yet its conclusion states the opposite), and with that sign D is minus the gradient and then the line-search trial points, not the update, are wrong. Either reading leaves one sign error and an ascent/undescent step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt one sign convention throughout: either keep eq:opt_system-b's terminal condition and change the update to ε^(j+1) ← Π_E(ε^(j) − σ^(j+1) D^(j)), or keep the update and change the Armijo trial points to Π_E(ε + τD); and make the appendix derivation and its identification of ∂^#_ε J̃ agree with that convention.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:dal (and Algorithm alg:admm, which calls it) is not a descent method as written: the Armijo decrease condition is imposed on one direction and the opposite direction is taken, so the convergence criteria of rmk:convergence (and the cost-decrease-based stopping rule) do not apply; the sign of the derived costate and of the discrete control gradient is ambiguous.
issues.title: Costate/gradient sign convention used inconsistently: DAL update is opposite to its line-searched direction
issues.why_classification: A set of local sign corrections restores a genuine descent step and leaves the optimality system's solution set (invariant under λ↦−λ), the structure of both algorithms and every guarantee intact, with no new argument or construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: One should ensure that the compact set $E$ is large enough to allow both global interactions, i.e. $\phi(r_{ij}^\varepsilon)>0$ for any $i,j = 1,\ldots,N$, and no interactions at all, i.e. $\phi(r_{ij}^\varepsilon)=0$ for all $i,j = 1,\ldots,N$.
each agent tends to align its state $c_i$ with the states of nearby agents whose intensities are similar
This behaviour can be encoded by an interaction kernel which quantifies the attraction between two agents as a function of both their spatial and tonal distances.

issues.failure_explanation: The given polynomial satisfies φ(0) = (0−1)(1−0)^4 = −1 and φ(r)<0 on [0,1/4). Since r_ij is small exactly for spatially close agents of similar colour, the term φ(r_ij)(c_j−c_i) then pushes c_i away from c_j: near-consensus configurations are linearly unstable (all weights negative give an anti-diffusion operator), contradicting the stated attraction/alignment mechanism and the clustering/consensus interpretation. Moreover Remark rmk:parameters' requirement φ(r_ij^ε)>0 for any i,j is unsatisfiable with this kernel, because r_ii=0 gives φ(r_ii)=φ(0)=−1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the kernel by a nonnegative compactly supported (Wendland-type) profile, e.g. (4r+1)(1−r)^4 on [0,1], so that φ ≥ 0 with φ(0)>0; everything else is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: With the kernel as written the model does not align similar agents and its clustering/quantization behaviour (including the cited convergence-to-clusters claim and the consensus regime discussed for small α) is not the one described; the experiments cannot be reproducing this kernel.
issues.title: Interaction kernel has a negative lobe, turning alignment into repulsion of similar agents
issues.why_classification: A short local fix of the kernel's sign/profile restores the attraction mechanism and makes the stated interaction regimes reachable, preserving every claim and guarantee without new arguments.

the term $\int_\Omega \mu \cdot (v^*-\nabla u^*)$ vanishes, so that any $\mu \in L^2(\Omega; \R^2)$ becomes feasible.
Despite this change, various results in the literature prove existence and uniqueness of a minimiser for \eqref{eq:cost_TV}, see for instance \cite{CL_1997}.
L(u,v,\mu) = \int_\Omega |v(x)| + \mu(x) \cdot (v(x) - \nabla u(x)) + \frac{\rho}{2} |v(x) - \nabla u(x)|^2 + \frac{\alpha}{2}(u(x)- I(x))^2\ dx.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The coercivity step is false: taking v_n = ∇u_n with u_n a piecewise-linear spike (height 1 on an interval of length n^{-2}, decreasing linearly to 0) gives L(u_n,v_n,μ) = ∫|∇u_n| + (α/2)‖u_n−I‖² bounded (the terms in μ cancel because v_n−∇u_n=0) while ‖(u_n,v_n)‖_{H¹×L²}→∞; the quadratic term controls only v−∇u and |v| grows at most linearly. Hence there is no weakly compact sublevel set and neither the direct-method step nor the minimax theorem invoked from ET_1999 (whose hypotheses — coercivity/compactness of one domain — are violated) applies. (ii) The statement itself is false as written: since μ ranges over all of L², sup_μ L(u,v,μ)<∞ forces v = ∇u, so a saddle point exists only if K attains its minimum on H¹. For edge-type data it does not: with Ω=(0,1)² and data I(x,y)=χ_{(0,1/2)}(x) the problem separates and the ROF minimiser is (1−2/α)χ_{(0,1/2)} + (2/α)χ_{(1/2,1)} for α>4 (the range used in the experiments), a jump function outside H¹; inf_{H¹}K = 1−2/α is not attained and no saddle point exists in H¹×L²×L². The paper's own reference places existence theory for eq:cost_TV in BV, not H¹.

failure_location.quote: Finally, as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:existence1}, it is immediate to show coercivity in the primal variables, ensuring that the minimum is attained in a weakly compact set.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate and re-prove the result in the natural setting for the ROF functional (u ∈ BV(Ω) with the splitting variable in the space of Radon measures and the quadratic penalty interpreted accordingly), obtaining existence of a saddle point and zero duality gap by convex duality; alternatively keep H¹ but replace min/max by inf/sup and add hypotheses on I and α guaranteeing attainment of the H¹ minimiser.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of a saddle point and the min–max (no-duality-gap) identity are unproved and, for the sharp-edge data the TV model is designed for, false in the stated spaces; the subsequent assertion that Theorem thm:saddle_point 'ensures that there is no duality gap' (used to justify the ADMM stopping rule) and the attainment of the primal pair (u*,v*) are unreliable.
issues.title: Saddle-point existence theorem unproved and false in the stated spaces (false coercivity; non-attainment for edge-type data)
issues.why_classification: More than a local fix: the asserted coercivity is false and the minimax theorem is used outside its hypotheses, so the statement must be weakened or moved to a BV/measure setting and re-proved. But the proof architecture (convexity + compactness + minimax) survives in the corrected spaces and the zero-duality-gap guarantee actually used downstream is preserved recognizably, so no major loss or new global theory is forced.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the statement to (possible) convergence to a stationary/local solution of the non-convex control problem, consistent with the paper's own caveat, and restrict the no-duality-gap/attainment statements to the convex relaxation over free (u,v).
